headline: September CPI at 8:30 decides whether an October Fed hike is back on the table
summary: The S&P 500 finished Tuesday flat at 7,805, just under its record close. A memory-chip selloff offset mostly solid bank earnings, and this morning futures are modestly higher with Dow contracts leading. The session turns on the 8:30 AM ET September CPI: economists expect headline inflation to rise to 3.6% on fuel costs, and a core reading above the 0.2% forecast would revive bets on a hike at the Oct. 27–28 Fed meeting while the 10-year yield already sits at 5.22%. Leadership is narrow (energy, health care and software), which favors staying with those trends and waiting for the number before adding to rate-sensitive groups.

fed.note: Before CPI, futures priced about a 22% chance of a quarter-point hike; Williams sees at most one more hike this year.

drivers.title: CPI decides the October Fed question
drivers.body: Economists expect September CPI to show headline inflation rising to 3.6% from 3.4% on a 0.6% monthly jump, with core up 0.2% (2.5% from a year earlier). The Fed raised its range to 3.75%–4.00% in September, and before the data futures priced roughly a 22% chance of another hike at the Oct. 27–28 meeting. New York Fed President Williams says one more hike this year may be appropriate but sees no need for hikes in 2027.

drivers.title: Bank profits strong, stock reactions muted
drivers.body: Goldman earned $17.01 a share against about $13.65 expected. JPMorgan missed ($5.57 vs. $5.90), Wells Fargo fell about 3% on a revenue shortfall, and Citi slipped despite a beat. This morning BlackRock reported adjusted EPS of $15.93 (up 38%) and $205.5 billion of net inflows, while Bank of America trades 1.5% lower premarket after a $1.21 billion regulatory fine.

drivers.title: War premium keeps Brent above $106
drivers.body: A Houthi strike hit a Saudi Aramco building in Dhahran, and Iranian forces struck two more ships near Hormuz on Tuesday, holding Brent near $106 after a gain of more than 14% in September. Refined fuels are tighter than crude, and the IEA expects diesel to stay tight into next year. That helps producers and refiners but weighs on fuel-heavy industries and the inflation outlook.

drivers.title: Memory-chip rout pauses as ASML guides higher
drivers.body: China's CXMT said it has made progress on a denser DRAM design, which sent SK Hynix down 10% and the Philadelphia chip index lower for a fifth straight session. Applied Materials fell about 7.5% after giving no industry spending forecast at its investor day. Overnight, ASML narrowed its 2026 sales outlook to €44–45 billion, guided Q4 to €14.2–15.2 billion and warned that supply may not meet demand for two years; Asian chip stocks steadied.

drivers.title: Yields near 2002 highs squeeze rate-sensitive stocks
drivers.body: The 10-year Treasury yield is at 5.22%, close to its highest level since 2002, and the 30-year mortgage rate reached 7.4%, the highest since November 2023. Fed Governor Waller said high long-term yields are already tightening conditions in housing and autos. The strain shows in homebuilders, REITs and small caps, with the Russell 2000 down 3.8% in a month.

drivers.title: Health care and software lead the tape
drivers.body: UnitedHealth beat estimates and raised its 2026 outlook to at least $20.50 a share, crediting tighter medical-cost control, which lifted managed care. Microsoft closed at a record after unveiling its Maia 300 AI chip, and software (IGV up 18% in three months) is holding up while semiconductors slide.

risks.title: A hot core CPI print
risks.body: A core reading of 0.3% or more, against 0.2% expected, would likely push October hike odds well above the roughly 22% priced before the data and lift yields again.

risks.title: Yields near 24-year highs
risks.body: The 10-year at 5.22% is close to its highest since 2002, and stocks and bonds have been falling together. Real estate, homebuilders and small caps feel it first.

risks.title: Oil shock cuts both ways
risks.body: More attacks on Saudi or Hormuz shipping could push Brent higher and feed inflation. A ceasefire or Hormuz reopening could quickly unwind the energy and refiner rally, as a Sept. 22 reopening report did to defense stocks.

risks.title: AI chip wobble spreads
risks.body: Memory is at the center of the selloff after CXMT's DRAM progress and warnings about AI funding. A weak TSMC outlook Thursday could pull software and hardware leaders down with it.

risks.title: Thin breadth under a near-record index
risks.body: Only 40% of S&P 500 members and 29% of midcaps are above their 50-day while the index sits 0.2% from its high, so a handful of leaders are carrying it.

avoid.name: Homebuilders
avoid.detail: ITB is down 12.9% in three months and no homebuilder in the scan is above its 200-day, with 30-year mortgages at 7.4%, the highest since November 2023.

avoid.name: Aerospace & defense
avoid.detail: ITA is down 13.6% in three months, only 10% of the industry is above its 200-day, and Boeing, Lockheed and RTX are in downtrends ahead of Oct. 20–27 reports.

avoid.name: Solar
avoid.detail: TAN is down 20.5% in three months and trades 18.8% below its 200-day average.

avoid.name: Airlines
avoid.detail: JETS is down 14.2% in three months and only 20% of carriers are above their 200-day as jet fuel tracks the diesel squeeze.

avoid.name: Packaged foods
avoid.detail: Only 18% of packaged-food stocks are above their 200-day, making it one of the 10 weakest industries in the scan.

avoid.name: Netflix
avoid.detail: In a downtrend 43% below its high, with relative strength near the bottom of the market, ahead of Oct. 20 earnings.

sectors.name: Energy
sectors.note: The strongest sector in the scan: 76% of members are above their 50-day average, the median stock is up 11% in three months, and refiners are at record highs. Attacks on Saudi targets and Hormuz shipping keep Brent above $106 and diesel tight; a ceasefire is the main risk.

sectors.name: Health Care
sectors.note: 77% of the sector is above its 200-day average, and UnitedHealth's raised 2026 outlook gave managed care a fresh reason to rally. Every life-science tools stock is above its 200-day; biotech (XBI down 6% in three months) is the weak spot.

sectors.name: Information Technology
sectors.note: Software and hardware carry the sector: 91% of systems-software names are above their 200-day average and Microsoft is at a record. Memory and chip-equipment stocks are being sold on CXMT's progress, so the scan favors software and hardware over memory until TSMC reports Thursday.

sectors.name: Consumer Staples
sectors.note: The sector is split. Beverages and tobacco (Coca-Cola, Philip Morris) trade near highs, while only 18% of packaged-food stocks are above their 200-day as input costs climb. The leaders hold up; the broad group does not.

sectors.name: Utilities
sectors.note: Half the group is above its 50-day but only 29% are above their 200-day, because a 5.22% 10-year yield competes with utility dividends. NorthWestern and Black Hills are at highs with RSI near 70, so no pick here until they pull back; power producers Vistra and Constellation remain more than 20% below their highs.

sectors.name: Financials
sectors.note: Only 19% of the sector is above its 50-day average and the median stock is down 6.3% in a month: JPMorgan missed, Wells Fargo's revenue fell short and Bank of America took a $1.21 billion fine. Life insurers and reinsurers, which reinvest bond portfolios at higher yields, are the exception and supply the one pick here.

sectors.name: Materials
sectors.note: Breadth is poor (18% above the 50-day), and no construction-materials stock is above its 200-day as 7.4% mortgages weigh on housing. Copper is the exception: it is up 5.7% in a month, and China's factory-gate inflation jumped to 5.0%.

sectors.name: Real Estate
sectors.note: The weakest breadth in the market: 10% of REITs are above their 50-day and 27% above their 200-day, as Treasury yields near 2002 levels and mortgages at their highest since November 2023 raise funding costs. Hotel REITs (Host, Park) are the only clean uptrends.

sectors.name: Industrials
sectors.note: Just 24% of the sector is above its 50-day. Aerospace and defense, airlines and transports are in downtrends as fuel costs bite and Hormuz-reopening headlines undercut the defense trade. Distributors and freight forwarders (MSC, Expeditors, Fastenal) are the groups still making highs.

sectors.name: Communication Services
sectors.note: 36% of the sector is above its 50-day and the median stock is down 5.2% in a month; Netflix is 43% below its high ahead of Oct. 20 earnings. Meta is the standout but sits about 18% above its 50-day, too stretched to chase.

sectors.name: Consumer Discretionary
sectors.note: The weakest sector by trend: 29% of members are above their 50-day and the median stock is down 8.1% in three months, with homebuilders, auto retail and casinos at the bottom of the industry ranks. High fuel prices and 7.4% mortgages squeeze households; Abercrombie and SharkNinja are isolated leaders.

picks.name: Chevron Corporation
picks.thesis: Integrated majors are a steadier way to own an oil market where Houthi attacks on Saudi facilities and Hormuz tanker strikes keep Brent above $106. A credible Saudi-Houthi ceasefire or a close below the risk line would undercut the setup.

picks.name: ConocoPhillips
picks.thesis: Producers (XOP up about 22% in three months) turn elevated crude directly into cash flow, and ConocoPhillips is consolidating just under its high. A sharp oil reversal or a drop back below the 50-day would invalidate it.

picks.name: Humana
picks.thesis: UnitedHealth's beat and raised outlook, credited to tighter medical-cost control, eases cost fears across Medicare Advantage, and Humana trends just below its high. A break of the risk line would end the setup.

picks.name: AbbVie
picks.thesis: AbbVie's immunology drugs (Rinvoq, Skyrizi) give it growth that does not depend on the economy, and the stock is in a steady uptrend just below its high. A close below the risk line would invalidate it.

picks.name: Charles River Laboratories
picks.thesis: Every life-science tools stock in the scan is above its 200-day, and Charles River sits in a buy zone just under its high. Slipping back below the 50-day would signal the group's run is tiring.

picks.name: Microsoft
picks.thesis: Microsoft hit a record as investors see its in-house Maia 300 AI chip as a cost advantage, and software has held up while chips sold off. RSI is near stretched levels, so dips toward the 50-day before Oct. 28 earnings are cleaner entries; a close below the risk line would invalidate it.

picks.name: Nutanix
picks.thesis: Systems software is the second-strongest industry in the scan, and Nutanix is consolidating just below its high. A drop below the 50-day would signal the rotation into software is fading.

picks.name: Coca-Cola Company (The)
picks.thesis: A defensive leader near its high while markets weigh another Fed hike; beverages have held up as packaged foods slide. Oct. 27 results are the next test, and a close below the risk line would invalidate it.

picks.name: Philip Morris International
picks.thesis: Pricing power in tobacco and smoke-free products suits an inflationary tape, and the uptrend sits near its high ahead of Oct. 21 earnings. A break of the risk line would invalidate it.

picks.name: MetLife
picks.thesis: Life insurers reinvest large bond portfolios at better rates when yields rise, so MetLife is at a high while banks lag. A sharp fall in long-term yields or a close below the risk line would weaken the case.

picks.name: Expeditors International
picks.thesis: A rare industrial at an all-time high, helped by demand for customs and trade-compliance work while transports overall slide. A move back below the 50-day would suggest the run has played out.

picks.name: MSC Industrial Direct
picks.thesis: Industrial distributors are holding up while the broader sector struggles, and MSC is at a new high ahead of Oct. 22 earnings. Fastenal's report this morning is a read-through for the group; a poor reaction there or a close below the risk line would be a warning.

picks.name: Freeport-McMoRan
picks.thesis: Copper is up 5.7% in a month and China's factory-gate prices rose more than expected, and Freeport sits right on its 50-day in a buy zone. The risk line is close, so a decisive break below it would invalidate the setup quickly.

picks.name: Valero Energy
picks.thesis: Refining is the scan's top industry because of a global diesel shortage the IEA expects to last into next year, and Valero hit an all-time high Tuesday. It is far above its 50-day, so a pullback before Oct. 22 earnings is the better entry; a peace deal that eases diesel would hurt.

picks.name: Dynatrace
picks.thesis: Dynatrace broke to new highs after RBC raised its target and the company reached a federal cloud-security milestone, but the stock is well above its 50-day. A pullback toward that average before its November report would be a better entry.

watchlist.name: Micron Technology
watchlist.trigger: A close back above the 50-day after TSMC's Thursday results; a firm TSMC AI outlook would ease the CXMT supply scare hitting memory.

watchlist.name: Applied Materials
watchlist.trigger: Reclaiming the 50-day would mark the end of the post-investor-day selloff; ASML's tight-supply warning supports equipment demand.

watchlist.name: Lam Research
watchlist.trigger: Oct. 21 earnings: a spending outlook that confirms ASML's tight-supply view, followed by a close above the 50-day.

watchlist.name: Intel
watchlist.trigger: Trading just below its 50-day; a close above it before Oct. 29 earnings would put it back in an uptrend.

watchlist.name: Comfort Systems USA
watchlist.trigger: The data-center contractor is about 21% off its high; a move back above the 50-day after Oct. 22 earnings.
